voiceScript: The biggest multi-factor authentication mistake starts with one rushed decision. Multi-Factor Authentication means the real-world choices, risks, and protections involved in multi-factor authentication. Picture this: a phone owner encounters multi-factor authentication during a normal day and must decide whether to trust a request, setting, or device. Here is why that matters: a rushed multi-factor authentication choice can expose information, interrupt access, or give the wrong person an opening.
